newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada tobacco restrictions approved in principle.
newsitem.headline: Canada tobacco restrictions approved in principle.

text.p: The Canadian House of Commons overwhelmingly approved in principle tough new restrictions on tobacco on Thursday.
Parliament's elected chamber voted 173-15 for the government bill and turned it over to committee for consideration.

The committee can change it and then the House will be asked to take a final vote before submitting it to the unelected Senate, where Health Minister David Dingwall said he had been warned the tobacco lobby might try to stall his bill.
The package seeks to ban tobacco advertisements on radio, television or billboards, prohibit vending machine sales, and restrict the use of brand names in sponsoring sporting and other events.
His bill was introduced in tandem with an increase in taxes in Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia.
